# Explain GPU Register Spills and Their Performance Cost

[← AMD](../README.md) · [Every AMD question](../../amd.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/explain-gpu-register-spills-and-their-performance-cost)

---

Define a GPU kernel register spill, explain why it occurs, and describe how you would check whether it is hurting performance.

### Constraints & Assumptions
Consider compiler-controlled per-thread registers and the backing storage when values can no longer stay in registers. Avoid mixing up a spill with programmer-declared shared or local scratchpad; terminology differs across programming environments.

### Clarifying Questions
What is the kernel’s register usage and live-variable pressure? Are registers the occupancy bottleneck? Does the compiler emit spill diagnostics? What memory traffic and stalls show up in profiling?

### What a Strong Answer Covers
Live intervals, limited register budget, spill load/store operations, occupancy tradeoffs, and changes supported by measured data.

### Follow-up Questions
Could forcing a lower register limit make a kernel slower? How can unrolling or large local arrays affect pressure? When might recomputation be cheaper than preserving a value?

Overview:
Explain GPU register spills through live-variable pressure, compiler register allocation, spill memory traffic, occupancy tradeoffs, and optimization choices backed by measurement.
